flags.sentence: It is debated whether Pachycephalosaurus used its dome for head-butting like bighorn sheep or for flank-butting like kangaroos.
flags.reason: The sentence presents the debate as an open question ('It is debated whether...'), but the quote explicitly states that the head-butting hypothesis 'has been widely hypothesized for decades' and frames the alternative (flank-butting) as a comparison to kangaroos without stating it is the debated alternative in the same way. More critically, the quote only supports the 'head-butting' hypothesis; it does not provide evidence or phrasing that supports the 'flank-butting' hypothesis as a valid, debated alternative in the source text. The sentence merges a settled hypothesis (head-butting) with an unmentioned alternative (flank-butting) into a balanced debate that the quote does not support.

flags.sentence: Se debate si Pachycephalosaurus utilizaba su bóveda para chocar con la cabeza como los carneros de cornamenta o para embestir los flancos como los canguros.
flags.reason: The Spanish translation changes the meaning by presenting the flank-butting hypothesis as a valid alternative ('o para embestir los flancos'), whereas the English source text and the quote only support the head-butting hypothesis. The quote does not mention flank-butting as a hypothesis, so the Spanish sentence introduces a claim not present in the source material.
